clips.title: What is Kubernetes | Kubernetes explained in 15 mins
clips.why: Nana explains the problem Kubernetes was made for: many containers on many machines, and somebody has to keep them running.
look: The move from one big application to many small containers, which is where the agent platform is: a gateway, a broker, a worker, a Slack app.
High availability and disaster recovery: the service keeps answering while machines fail. That is the 3 a.m. story of this lesson.
Notice that every feature she lists is something you would otherwise do by hand with docker run.
clips.after: On inf, the machines really do come and go, because they are Spot nodes, so the broker depends on these features every week.

clips.title: Kubernetes Components explained! Pods, Services, Secrets, ConfigMap | Kubernetes Tutorial 14
clips.why: The clearest drawing of the two ideas in this lesson: a pod gets a new IP every time it is replaced, and a Service gives it a name that stays.
look: Each pod gets its own IP address, and a replacement pod gets a new one. That is why nothing may store a pod's IP.
The Service has a permanent address, and its life is not tied to the pods behind it.
Internal versus external Services: our broker's Service is internal (ClusterIP). You can stop when she moves on to Ingress.
clips.after: broker.ai-agents is exactly her internal Service: the orchestrator calls that name, and it keeps working however often the broker's pods change.

clips.title: Kubernetes Pods, ReplicaSets, and Deployments in 5 Minutes
clips.why: A short, exact explanation of why you create Deployments instead of pods, and of the control loop that keeps the count true.
look: A ReplicaSet keeps a number of identical pods running, and a Deployment manages ReplicaSets so it can change the image step by step.
The control loop: observe what is running, compare it with what you asked for, act on the difference, and repeat.
The YAML on screen has the same three parts as the broker's Deployment: replicas, selector and template.
clips.after: The broker's Deployment on inf asks for 2 replicas, and this loop is what brought the second copy back at 3 in the morning.

practice.q: You want the broker to keep running as two copies, even when a node disappears. What do you create?

options.text: Two pods with the broker image
options.why: Nothing replaces a bare pod when it dies. You would be back to restarting things by hand.
The Deployment is the desired state. The control loop keeps two pods running from its template, whatever happens to the nodes.
A Service only gives pods a name; it never starts or replaces a pod.

practice.q: Finish the broker's Service so that it sends calls to the broker's pods.
practice.hint: It must be exactly the label in the Deployment's pod template.
practice.why: The selector must match the pods' label exactly. One wrong letter and the Service has no endpoints, so every call fails while the pods look perfectly healthy.

practice.q: A node disappears at 3 in the morning. Put what happens in order.
items: The node and the broker pod on it disappear
The control loop sees one broker pod where the Deployment asks for two
It creates a new pod from the template, with a new name and a new IP
The new pod answers GET /health and becomes ready
The Service adds the new pod's IP to its endpoints, and calls to broker.ai-agents reach it
practice.why: The Deployment restores the count and the Service follows the label. Nobody's config changes, because callers only know the Service name.

practice.q: kubectl get pods says No resources found, but you are sure the broker is running. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The broker crashed and was deleted
options.why: A crashed pod still shows, with a status like CrashLoopBackOff, and the Deployment would start a new one.

options.text: You forgot -n ai-agents, so kubectl looked in the default namespace
options.why: Without -n, kubectl uses the namespace called default, which is empty. This is the most common moment of panic with kubectl.

options.text: kubectl get pods only lists pods you created yourself
options.why: It lists every pod in the namespace you ask about, whoever created it.

practice.q: Inside the cluster, which DNS name reaches the Service broker in the namespace ai-agents? (short form)
practice.hint: Service name, a dot, then the namespace.
practice.why: A Service's name is the Service plus the namespace: broker.ai-agents, short for broker.ai-agents.svc.cluster.local. From inside the same namespace, plain broker works too.
